newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 8.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Allegheny Power agreed to acquire DQE Inc for $2.51 billion in stock. It would also assume $1.7 billion in debt and preferred stock.
* Federal Communications Commission Reed Hundt wants to postpone a key step in changing subsidies which keep U.S. phone service affordable until next year.
* Rational Software said it would buy Pure Atria in a stock swap initially valued at $844 million, but both companies' shares fell sharply.
* A federal probe into Columbia/HCA's operations in El Paso, Texas focuses largely on physician referrals to the company's home health-care agencies.
* Analysts say the outlook for Ford and General Motors profits is improving.
* As part of its probe of alcohol advertising, the Federal Trade Commission is looking at television ad campaigns by Anheuser-Busch and Philip Morris's Miller Brewing.
* Investors are buying shares of midsize specialty securities firm after Bankers Trust announced plans to buy Alex. Brown for $1.7 billion.
* The Philadelphia Stock Exchange is investigating unusual trading in options on Alex. Brown shares before the takeover announcement.
* The Dow Jones industrials rose 29.84 to 6,555.91.
* USX-US Steel and Inland Steel said they talked about a possible combination last year but decided against going ahead with a deal.
* Motorola reported better-than-anticipated quarterly profits although net income and net margins declined from year-ago levels.
* Ford Chairman Alex Trotman's received $5.1 million in total compensation in 1996 although his bonus was cut.
* Advanced Micro Devices posted revenue gains in three key business areas and an unexpected quarterly profit.
* Kodak, mulling the possibility of making Kodak film in China, is talking to several Chinese photo firms.

* Heard on the Street: Investors scrambled to snap up shares of midsize, specialty securities companies yesterday after news that Bankers Trust New York plans to buy Baltimore's Alex. Brown Inc for $1.7 billion.
* Bond prices shrugged off their recent slump to post sharp gains, helped by strength in the dollar and short-covering by traders.
